decisions.D6_final: OWNER, 2026-09-15, a nine-answer quiz; it replaces D1 and the supervisor D6. Q1 nothing is refused because of a subshell. Q2 a warning only when the loss is CERTAIN: `each` with an INSTANCE-member callback (detected by `[[ $cb == *.* ]] && declare -p "${cb%%.*}_data"`), `toArray`, `toList`; `each` with a plain function or a static member, and `first`/`count`, are silent. Q3 two per-call silencers: the flag -s (sugar) and the dynamically scoped KK_SUBSHELL_OK=1 (the primitive, survives a wrapper). Q4 the names mean 'the subshell scope is intended' and the variable is kcl-wide (KK_). Q5 one line per call, no de-duplication. Q7 TPipe.each never prints RESULT — its stdout is the callback's; RESULT is still set on a direct call. Q8 'a subshell is unavoidable and the state must come back' = documented recipes plus a kklass roadmap item (snapshot/restore of an instance); nothing in TPipe. Q9 TUtil gets `var subshellOk` (tutil PLAN P4).

execution_log.batch: P3 — D6 final (owner ruling), with kkore kk.warn and tutil P4
execution_log.summary: Opus worker, reviewer verification pending. THE RULE: D1 (stdin form in a subshell = rc 2) and the P0 D6 (a kk.debug line for the -- form) are both gone; a sink in a subshell is never refused, and when the loss is CERTAIN it prints ONE kk.warn line and proceeds with exactly the contract's rc and RESULT. Certain = `each` whose callback is an INSTANCE member (`[[ $cb == *.* ]] && declare -p "${cb%%.*}_data"`, a builtin, no fork, only on the warning path), `toArray` (the nameref fill cannot reach the caller) and `toList` (INST.Add mutates a list nobody will see); `each` with a plain function or a STATIC member, and `first`/`count`, are silent. Two templates keyed on the FORM: the stdin form names `shopt -s lastpipe` and the `TPipe.MEMBER [OPERAND] -- CMD ...` form, the `--` form says 'move the call out of $( ) / ( )'; both end 'if the subshell scope is intended, pass -s or set KK_SUBSHELL_OK=1'. Silencers: the flag `-s` (accepted by every sink, inert on first/count) and the dynamically scoped KK_SUBSHELL_OK=1 (per call as a prefix assignment, per block as a `local`) — the variable is the primitive and reaches TPipe through TGrep/TUtil with no wrapper code. Q5: one line per call, no de-duplication. Q6: the line goes through the NEW shared helper kk.warn (kkore/klib.sh), i.e. it is printed with the debug switch OFF and silenced by VERBOSE_KKLASS=quiet — a corpus rule, written up in kcl/README.md §1.2. Q7: TPipe.each never prints — it answers `RESULT=$n; return $rc` and never calls tpipe._ret, so `x=$(TPipe.each fmt -- cmd)` and `TPipe.each fmt -- cmd | sort` carry exactly the callback's bytes (before: the record count was appended in both positions); a direct call still sets RESULT. Q8: recipes only, plus a kklass roadmap pointer (snapshot/restore of an instance); nothing in TPipe. Q9: tutil `var subshellOk` -> `-s` (tutil ledger P4).
